subject: Clarification on incident notice timing, cross-border cooperation, and foreign-law carve-outs
messages:
From: Sara Klein <sara.klein@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Legal <legal@acme.com>, Fintegral Security <security@fintegral.com>
Date: 2028-05-23T09:12:00Z
Subject: Incident notification — timing & cross-border cooperation questions

Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — ACME is excited about the latency and cost profile. Before we proceed to procurement we need to clarify several points in the DPA related to incident notifications and evidence sharing. Our security team (Fintegral) attached an initial question matrix (sent separately). High-level items: 

- Our legal/regulatory team needs a clear maximum notification window for "confirmed unauthorized access affecting ACME personal data"; can Redwood commit to a 48-hour notice after confirmation, or do you require an exception?
- If Redwood's investigation requires transferring logs or forensic images to a Redwood partner in another jurisdiction, what process do you propose for cross-border transfer and minimization?
- How does Redwood handle requests from foreign law enforcement that might conflict with EU data export restrictions?

Could you loop in privacy and security so we can get concrete language for the DPA? We want to avoid open-ended terms that could delay procurement.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — ACME is targeting a signature by June.

Best,
Sara Klein
Sr. Contracts Manager, ACME Corp

Attachments: ACME_DPA_questions.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sara Klein <sara.klein@acme.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-23T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Incident notification — timing & cross-border cooperation questions

Sara — thanks for the clear matrix and timeline. Looping in legal (Kimberly), privacy (Ben), security (Grace) and your CS contact (Marissa) to align. Quick answers up front:

- Notification window: our standard commitment in the hosted contract is "as soon as reasonably practicable and not later than 72 hours after confirmation". We can discuss a 48-hour target for higher-tier Dedicated/Private customers but that requires SLA/operational changes (and an escalation path).
- Cross-border transfer: we minimize by producing exported evidence via secure, regionally-hosted export locations where possible; transfers occur only with customer consent or pursuant to lawful request, and we prefer to use an encrypted transfer with access controls and an audit trail.
- Conflicting foreign-law requests: we treat these on a case-by-case basis with legal escalation; typically we notify the customer of legal process and seek to narrow scope, using protective measures where allowed.

Kim — can you propose redline language that: (1) sets a firm 72h standard, (2) offers a negotiable 48h SLA addendum for Dedicated/Private, and (3) includes a clause describing coordination on cross-border forensic exports and notice when a governmental demand arises?

Ben/Grace — can you confirm operational feasibility for a 48-hour confirmed-notify target and the controls we'd need to guarantee it (on-call rota, prioritized forensics, runbook link)?

Sara — we'll aim to get a draft back today.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of GTM Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sara Klein <sara.klein@acme.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-23T13:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Incident notification — proposed DPA redlines and cooperation language

Vanessa / Sara — attached is a suggested clause set (redwood_dpa_clause_suggestions.docx) and a PDF with brief commentary (DPA_v3_redlines.pdf). Key proposals summarized below for ease of review: 

1) Notification timing (Article X): 
   - "Redwood will provide Initial Notice to Customer no later than seventy-two (72) hours after Redwood reasonably confirms that an incident has occurred that has resulted in unauthorized access to Customer Personal Data. Initial Notice will include a summary of known impact, affected data categories, and immediate mitigation steps.
   - "For Dedicated or Private deployment customers that execute a Service Level Addendum, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide Initial Notice within forty‑eight (48) hours of confirmation; such 48‑hour target shall be subject to an agreed escalation playbook and staffing commitments."

2) Scope and evidence export: 
   - "Redwood will minimize cross-border transfers of forensic artifacts. Where forensic data must be transferred to a third‑party processor or subprocessor in another jurisdiction to support investigation, Redwood will: (a) notify Customer promptly; (b) provide a description of categories of data to be transferred; (c) ensure encryption in transit and at rest; and (d) limit recipients and retention consistent with the purpose of the investigation."

3) Foreign-law conflict handling: 
   - "If Redwood receives a request from a foreign governmental authority that would compel disclosure inconsistent with applicable data export or protection obligations, Redwood will: (a) notify Customer unless prohibited by law; (b) seek to narrow the scope; and (c) if compelled, Redwood will, to the extent permitted, provide only the minimum information required and document the legal process."

Operational asks for the 48h target (Ben/Grace): please confirm the following are available/feasible within the proposed SLA addendum: 
- 24/7 incident triage rotation with an identified primary forensics lead
- Dedicated prioritized forensic VM snapshot pipeline with encrypted transfer channel
- Pre-approved list of forensic subprocessor partners + template DPIA

Sara — if ACME is agreeable to the 72h default with an optional 48h addendum that includes staffing/pricing commitments, we can prepare a tracked-redline DPA and the SLA addendum for signature.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dpa_clause_suggestions.docx (docx); DPA_v3_redlines.pdf (pdf)

From: Sara Klein <sara.klein@acme.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Legal <legal@acme.com>, Fintegral Security <security@fintegral.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-23T15:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Incident notification — proposed DPA redlines and cooperation language

Kimberly — thanks for the clear draft and the operational checklist. A few ACME notes: 

- The 72h baseline is acceptable as a default. ACME is open to the 48h SLA addendum for Dedicated/Private deployments provided Redwood commits to the three operational items you've listed and we receive an estimated uplift in fees. Please include a concrete pricing delta in the SLA addendum.
- Regarding cross-border transfers: ACME requires that any transfer to a third party outside the EEA be limited to a list of pre-approved subprocessors and subject to execution of a mutual nondisclosure addendum. Can you provide your current subprocessor roster for forensic services and the proposed template DPIA?
- On foreign-law requests: ACME asks for a clause to permit an agreed escalation timeframe before production (48 hours) to allow ACME to seek protective relief, unless Redwood is prohibited from delaying by law. Is that acceptable to Redwood?

If you can provide the redlines and the subprocessor roster, we will route to procurement and legal — we still aim to sign by early June.

Best,
Sara Klein
Sr. Contracts Manager, ACME Corp
